_comment: Smoke configuration: all 48 conditions, a 4-case slice. Runs the full pipeline end to end so a failure surfaces in ~1-2h instead of 40 minutes into the real matrix. Verify a finished run with smoke_check.py. Never report numbers from this config - 4 cases measures nothing.
_seed_rationale: shuffle=true because limit takes rows[:N] and the first five testset entries are all order-management.json. Seed 12116 is a coverage device, not a measurement: its first four shuffled entries span four distinct logs INCLUDING bpic2017-ocel2.json, the 2.2 GB log most likely to fail on time or memory, at the lowest gold-execution cost of any seed satisfying that (40k seeds searched). The project seed 3407 covers four logs but misses bpic2017 entirely.
case_timeout_sec_note: Wall-clock budget per case, generation through execution. Calibrated 2026-08-19 from the 4056 pre-cap wave-1 records: p50=36.0 p90=85.9 p95=103.7 p99=157.8 max=377.0 sec. 600 is ~1.6x the observed maximum and ~3.8x p99, and sits above ocpq_cli_timeout_sec (300) so the backend's own timeout still fires first for a pure execution hang. It is therefore a bound on pathology, not a budget that trims the normal distribution: no observed case came within 220s of it. A cap tight enough to actually bind would have to sit below 300 and would make the CLI timeout unreachable.
max_result_file_gb_note: Refuse to parse a prediction's result export larger than this. Parsing costs a measured ~11.7x the file size in RAM and the whole file is read at once, so an over-selecting query SIGKILLs the shard -- uncatchable. Shard 60 of job 3087762 died this way at 64GB and again at 122GB (2026-08-21/25). 8GB projects to ~94GB resident, inside the 122GB ceiling with margin. Provably inert for the 95 shards that completed at 64GB: any export large enough to trip this would have needed ~94GB to parse and so would have OOM-killed them, and exactly one shard did.
